- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early or too high after sharp historical spikes, then overshoot and fail to correct downward.
- Mean reversion is underappreciated — model fails to recognize that prices often revert to lower levels after short-term spikes.
- Model exhibits lag in responding to recent downward trends; it often holds high forecasts even when recent data shows weakening momentum.
- Forecasts are overly optimistic in the middle of the 30-day horizon, especially when historical data shows volatility or consolidation.
- Model underreacts to low historical values near the end of the 30-day window — fails to adjust downward when recent prices are already low.
- Forecasts show persistent bias toward higher values, especially when historical data includes a recent high followed by a correction.
- Model tends to smooth out volatility, underestimating sharp downward corrections after spikes.
- Forecasts often overcorrect after a recent low, leading to a “rebound overshoot” that doesn’t align with true price behavior.
- Model fails to account for seasonal or cyclical patterns in the 30-day window, especially when prices are trending downward after a peak.
